As noted above, streams are considered to be pre-serialized, so they will be
sent unmodified without response validation.

See special note about error handling for streams in
[`setErrorHandler`](./Server.md#seterrorhandler).

Streams are piped to the response as they are, chunk by chunk. Over HTTP/2 all
the streams of a session share one connection, so emitting very large chunks
keeps the session busy with a single write, and cancelling such a response
leaves that write unfinished, stalling the other streams on the same session.
When serving large payloads over HTTP/2, emit them in reasonably sized chunks
(for example with `highWaterMark`) instead of a single large one. Buffers and
strings passed to `send` are chunked by Fastify already.

'Internal server error' : error.message) }) ``` Beware that calling `reply.send(error)` in your custom error handler will send the error to the default error handler. +Streams are piped to the response as they are, chunk by chunk. Over HTTP/2 all
+the streams of a session share one connection, so emitting very large chunks
+keeps the session busy with a single write, and cancelling such a response
+leaves that write unfinished, stalling the other streams on the same session.
+When serving large payloads over HTTP/2, emit them in reasonably sized chunks
+(for example with `highWaterMark`) instead of a single large one. Buffers and
+strings passed to `send` are chunked by Fastify already.

## What changed

**`lib/reply.js`** (hotspot — 38 past fixes)
- Added `HTTP2_MAX_CHUNK_SIZE` (16 KiB, the default HTTP/2 max frame size) with a comment explaining the failure mode: every stream of an HTTP/2 session shares one socket, so a single large queued write that the client then cancels leaves the session with a write it can never complete, stalling the other streams.
- In `onSendEnd`, the string/Buffer path now routes through a new `sendChunked()` when `req.raw.httpVersionMajor === 2` and the payload exceeds one frame. HTTP/1 and small HTTP/2 payloads keep the original single `res.write()` + `sendTrailer()` path unchanged.
- `sendChunked()` writes frame-sized slices, waits for `'drain'` when `res.write()` returns `false`, bails out if `res.destroyed` (so a cancelled stream drops the remainder instead of leaving it queued), and sends trailers only after the full payload is written. Strings are encoded to a Buffer once up front so slicing can't cut a multi-byte character in half; Buffers are sliced with `subarray`, so no copy.

**`docs/Reference/Reply.md`** — note under "Streams" that user-provided streams are piped through as-is, and that apps serving large payloads over HTTP/2 should emit reasonably sized chunks rather than one big one; Buffers and strings passed to `send` are already chunked by Fastify.

**`test/http2/plain.test.js`** — new `http2 large buffer payload` test: a 1 MiB buffer arrives byte-identical over the chunked path, and after cancelling a large response mid-flight with `NGHTTP2_CANCEL`, a subsequent request on the same session still succeeds.

## Risk-map partners (per COMPLEX.md)
- **`lib/request.js`** (co-change 38%): opened; no change needed. It exposes `protocol` (http/https only) and nothing HTTP/2-version-related, so I read `req.raw.httpVersionMajor` directly — the same idiom already used in `lib/route.js:479`.
- **`lib/symbols.js`** (co-change 52%): opened; no change needed. The chunk size is a module constant, not per-reply state, so no new symbol.

- `node --test test/http2/plain.test.js` → 7/7 pass.
